chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no man who gathers his family and places a meal before him, and he says the name of Allah (Bismillah) and they say the name of Allah at the beginning of the food, and they praise Allah (Al-Hamdulillah) at its end, so the meal is raised while they are forgiven.'

key_terms.تَرْتَفِعُ: it is raised (referring to the meal being taken away)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of reciting Bismillah and Al-Hamdulillah during meals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain linking the Prophet to Imam al-Sadiq, underscoring the domestic sphere as a locus of spiritual elevation. The imagery of the table 'rising' signifies the ascent of the meal's blessings and the family's collective merit, transforming a mundane act of eating into a means of securing divine forgiveness through mindful remembrance.
